title: Which primes multiply to make twelve hundred?
description: One thousand two hundred is broken into primes with the division method, dividing by two four times, then by three and by five. The divisors and the last number are collected, repeats included. Keeko's doubt, writing each prime only once, is tested by multiplying.
teaching_notes: One idea: a prime that divides again and again is written as many times as it divides. Watch for students who write each prime once.

source: Find the prime factorisation of 1200 using the division meth
video_script.why: The child can use the division method on small numbers and now meets a longer chain with repeated primes.
video_script.substitution: Collect every divisor and the last number, writing each one as many times as it appears.
video_script.anchor: The number one thousand two hundred with a column of divisions, the primes on its left.
video_script.wrong_answer: each prime is written only once
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says each prime is written only once. But 2 x 3 x 5 is 30, not 1200, so the repeats must be kept.
video_script.payoff_line: One thousand two hundred is two times two times two times two times three times five times five.

final_answer.spoken: one thousand two hundred is two times two times two times two times three times five times five

maths_rules: Slip: 2 x 3 x 5 = 30, not 1200, so repeats must be kept.
video_script.design: One idea: collect every divisor and the last number, repeats included. Assumes the division method. Wrong idea: each prime is written once. The column of divisions stays on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card, From your book; the number 1200; the question is written below

marks.book: The title card From your book arrives and the number twelve hundred appears
marks.ask: The question is written below the number

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the number one thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you find its prime factorisation using the division method?

beats.on_screen: the number and the question stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a number divided by the same prime twice in a row, the prime written on the left each time

marks.repeat: The same prime is written twice on the left of a column
marks.write: Each answer is written below the number it came from

narration: <bookmark mark='repeat'/>The same prime may divide a number again and again.
<bookmark mark='write'/>Each time, write the prime on the left and the answer below, until a prime is left.

marks.given: The number is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number is one thousand two hundred.

beats.on_screen: To find: the prime factorisation of 1200

marks.find: The words To find are written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find its prime factorisation by dividing.

marks.twos: Two is written on the left of twelve hundred and six hundred is written below
marks.more: Three more twos are written on the left, with three hundred, one hundred and fifty and seventy five below

narration: <bookmark mark='twos'/>Step one, one thousand two hundred is even, so divide by two to get six hundred.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Divide by two again to get three hundred, then one hundred and fifty, then seventy five.

marks.odd: Seventy five is marked odd and three is written on its left with twenty five below
marks.five: Five is written on the left of twenty five and five is written below

narration: <bookmark mark='odd'/>Step two, seventy five is odd, so two no longer divides it. Divide by three to get twenty five.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Divide twenty five by five to get five, which is a prime, so we stop.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: collect the divisors and the last number: 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 5, 5

marks.collect: The primes on the left and the last number are circled and collected in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='collect'/>Step three, collect the primes along the left and the one at the bottom.
They are two four times, then three, then five twice.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1200 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 x 5

marks.ans: The answer is boxed in the highlight colour

beats.colours: the answer in the highlight colour
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>One thousand two hundred is two times two times two times two times three times five times five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the column
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 2 x 3 x 5 = 30 next to 1200; the bubble is struck through and the repeated primes are written back

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble with each prime written once appears
marks.miss: The product of those three primes is written and it does not match twelve hundred
marks.fix: The bubble is struck through and the repeated primes are written back

beats.colours: the wrong idea in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks each prime is written only once.
<bookmark mark='miss'/>Two times three times five is thirty, which is not one thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Each divisor stays in the product, including the repeats.
